name: Sugammadex
route_note: single IV bolus at the end of surgery or for immediate reversal
originator: Organon (Anton Bom, Mingqiang Zhang and colleagues, Newhouse, Scotland)

discovery.by: Anton Bom and colleagues, Organon Laboratories, Newhouse
discovery.note: A gamma-cyclodextrin with eight carboxyl thioether side chains was designed to encapsulate the steroid nucleus of rocuronium in a 1:1 complex.

tagline: Cyclodextrin that rapidly reverses rocuronium and vecuronium by encapsulation
summary: Sugammadex is a modified gamma-cyclodextrin that binds rocuronium and vecuronium tightly in plasma, rapidly reversing neuromuscular blockade without acting on acetylcholinesterase. It can reverse even deep block within minutes and has largely replaced neostigmine in many settings where cost allows.
mechanism: Sugammadex's ring-shaped molecule has a lipophilic cavity that encloses the steroid skeleton of rocuronium or vecuronium, forming a very stable 1:1 complex.

Capture of free drug in plasma creates a concentration gradient that pulls neuromuscular blocker away from the neuromuscular junction, restoring transmission. Because it does not increase acetylcholine, it avoids muscarinic effects and does not need co-administration of an anticholinergic.
uses: Reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium or vecuronium in adults and children

history.title: Design
history.detail: Organon scientists in Scotland design Org 25969 to encapsulate rocuronium.

history.title: Publication
history.detail: The concept is published, describing the first 'selective relaxant binding agent'.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Bridion authorised in the EU; the FDA declines approval over hypersensitivity and bleeding concerns.

history.title: Merck
history.detail: Merck & Co. gains the product through its merger with Schering-Plough, which had acquired Organon.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: FDA approves Bridion in December after further studies.

history.title: Paediatric approval
history.detail: FDA extends use to children aged two and older.

pk.excretion: renal, more than 90% unchanged within 24 hours

serious: recurrence of block with inadequate dosing

facts: It also binds progestogens, so hormonal contraceptive users should regard a dose as equivalent to a missed pill and use backup contraception for seven days.
